clinician.final_diagnosis: emphysematous pyelonephritis complicated by methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) bacteremia
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 60-year-old woman with acute-on-chronic right knee, left hip, and paraspinal lumbar back pain and urinary retention presented without diabetes or prior UTIs. Early after admission, she developed fever, tachycardia, and early shock, was started on broad-spectrum antibiotics including vancomycin and Zosyn, and underwent emergent percutaneous nephrostomy tube placement. Abdominal CT on admission revealed left renal staghorn calculus with intraparenchymal gas locules diagnostic of emphysematous pyelonephritis. Post-operatively, urine culture grew Escherichia coli. Blood cultures confirmed MRSA bacteremia complicating the infection. The clinical progression, imaging, microbiology, and interventions substantiate the diagnosis.
